title: Learning to write for the Hammond organ at NBC
summary: Given an odd instrumentation including Hammond organ, Budd buys an organ book and crams to write the parts.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah, see. I'm a staff arranger at NBC now, and I'm commissioned to do four arrangements a week. Well, I didn't know when -- what I had to do but I always had a little heart that I would try anything one time. So when he called me then we sat down in a little conference room and he was typing out what he was going to do. I said, what's your
instrumentation? He said, well Budd, I've got a Hammond organ, and a piano, clarinet accordion, bass clarinet, oboe, flute and horn. flugelhorn.

I said 'what?' What a combination when he said Hammond organ I said oh, my God. What am I going to do now, you know. So they had two white fellas and me, one black fella for the arranger. Now, the two white fellas were going to make between them three arrangements a week, I'm going to do four.
Do you know what their names were?

I don't even remember, I never came in contact with them again. In fact, I'm going to tell you something, they gave me my first assignment, my four arrangements. Okay. I'm saying how on earth do you write for the Hammond organ? So I spent the rest of that day trying to contact different arrangers that I knew, I mean good arrangers. Jesse Stone, Don Redman, everybody, I said, look -- I even went to Hammond Organ himself, I said I just wanted to see -- I know how the music is supposed to sound because I used to listen to Jesse Crawford and all of these cats, and I knew -- Hammond organ was beautiful, he was one of the greatest organists that ever lived.
Chicago Theatre, man. And he was on the radio and played all of this beautiful organ. I just used to turn him on and listen to that beautiful music. So I

know -- of course he wasn't playing a Hammond, he was playing that great big -- any way, I said what am I going to do? Nobody could tell me how to write for the Hammond Organ, and so finally I wind up at Carl Fisher's and -- on 57th Street, and I said have you got anything on Hammond Organ? Oh, yeah, they said, we have a new book that's just published. I said, well give it to me, how much is it? $5.00. I said, give it here, wrap it up.
So all I wanted to do was to see how the music was written.

Well, now, I got this book and I grabbed the subway. I'm going home now, it's evening, and I opened this book up and it's nothing but reading, there's not a note down there where I can see how it's written. Now I've got to read the book before I can write, and this is telling about the tone colors and the mixing and everything what you have to do. Okay, I read the book and I'm scanning, I'm scanning and trying to cram, you know, because I'm picking up this music on Monday, my deadline is Thursday. That means I've got four days, I've got to get the music to the copy so he can copy it and have it ready for the show.
